Architecture – What We Know & Understand Today

Designed as a traditional client-server architecture, the application and database reside on a central server, typically located at a dental office, and interact with end-user desktops (clients). While this model works well for single-office setups,
it struggles to support larger dental groups with more than 30 users
Frontend UI is built on C++ and PowerBuilder, technologies that are outdated and less commonly used in modern software development
making resources in the market difficult to find to maintain and update
Backend business logic is written in C++, but modernization efforts have introduced .NET 4.6, with plans to upgrade to .NET 4.8 in version 24.20. but many areas of the
application still rely on outdated 32-bit libraries
) posing challenges in transitioning to modern 64-bit systems
Application database is SQL Anywhere, a lightweight and self-contained database engine
support for this database is ending in January 2025
, prompting an extensive migration to a new database

, comprising the majority of the application's functionality across 1,500 stored procedures. This design limits scalability and makes the system unsuitable as the foundation for a web-based, multi-tenant application capable of supporting thousands of customers

exact_paragraphs.text:
POWERBUILDER RETIREMENT
PowerBuilder has become a niche, legacy application stack. West Monroe recommends modernizing to a web-based user interface layer to ensure Pattern can continue to hire skilled engineers, to support a potential SaaS-ification of the product, and alignment with potential desktop and mobile deployment capabilities.

exact_paragraphs.text:
THREE-TIER RESPONSIBILITY
Modern application architecture practices over the last 15 years recommend a 3-tier structure: data access, service/domain, and user interface to ensure each layer can be maintained and upgraded separately. West Monroe recommends aligning to this high-level approach as an outcome of the modernization.

exact_paragraphs.text:
JOURNEY-LED DELIVERY
By using a journey-led approach, the disruption inside individual critical user journeys is minimized. Piloting specific personas or roles holistically can create a more seamless transition experience for customers. In addition, end to end testing for specific flows can be aligned with the testing workstream.

to a classic 3-tier architecture and modernizing the user interface stack

West Monroe recommends taking a user-journey focused approach to the modernization program. But identifying and prioritizing user journeys, we can align the modernization and testing strategy approach to ensure that changes are desirable, performant and validated.
PowerBuilder supports a practice-local application where the user experience, business behavior, and data access have grown together.
The user experience remains tied to a legacy desktop runtime.
Business rules and transaction behavior span UI code and direct data paths.
Device and partner dependencies shape each journey transition.
Screen-only replacement preserves the existing business and data coupling.
An independent user experience, reusable business operations, governed data access, and a clear path to PowerBuilder retirement.

PowerBuilder has become a niche, legacy application stack. West Monroe recommends modernizing to a web-based user interface layer to ensure Pattern can continue to hire skilled engineers, to support a potential SaaS-
of the product, and alignment with potential desktop and mobile deployment capabilities.

r the last 15 years recommend a 3-tier structure: data access, service/domain, and user interface to ensure each layer can be maintained and upgraded separately. West Monroe recommends aligning to this high-level approach as an outcome of the modernization.

React provides browser or PWA delivery within the practice network. Embedded and desktop routes remain transition choices. WAN network support could potentially allow multi-site expansion for practices with that network capability.
By using a journey-led approach, the disruption inside individual critical user journeys is minimized.
specific personas or roles holistically can create a more seamless transition experience for customers. In addition, end to end testing for specific flows can be aligned with the testing workstream.

paragraphs.text:
POWERBUILDER RETIREMENT
PowerBuilder has become a niche, legacy application stack. West Monroe recommends modernizing to a web-based user interface layer to ensure Pattern can continue to hire skilled engineers, to support a potential SaaS-ification of the product, and alignment with potential desktop and mobile deployment capabilities.

paragraphs.text:
THREE-TIER RESPONSIBILITY
Modern application architecture practices over the last 15 years recommend a 3-tier structure: data access, service/domain, and user interface to ensure each layer can be maintained and upgraded separately. West Monroe recommends aligning to this high-level approach as an outcome of the modernization.

paragraphs.text:
WEB EXPERIENCE ON PREMISES
React provides browser or PWA delivery within the practice network. Embedded and desktop routes remain transition choices. WAN network support could potentially allow multi-site expansion for practices with that network capability.

paragraphs.text:
JOURNEY-LED DELIVERY
By using a journey-led approach, the disruption inside individual critical user journeys is minimized. Piloting specific personas or roles holistically can create a more seamless transition experience for customers. In addition, end to end testing for specific flows can be aligned with the testing workstream.

CORE RECOMMENDATION
Identify end-to-end user journeys for PowerBuilder retirement. After a journey meets acceptance criteria, retire its screen and runtime, rebuild its UI logic in React, and route business rules and data access through the API and data access layers.

paragraphs.text:
CORE RECOMMENDATION
Identify end-to-end user journeys for PowerBuilder retirement. After a journey meets acceptance criteria, retire its screen and runtime, rebuild its UI logic in React, and route business rules and data access through the API and data access layers.

Recommended target architecture for Eaglesoft user journeys
Identify end-to-end user journeys and define acceptance criteria
Retire each screen and runtime only after its journey is accepted
Rebuild UI logic in React + TypeScript
Route business rules through API and domain services
Centralize PostgreSQL access and preserve on-premises documents and imaging
Modernize one complete user journey at a time; retire its PowerBuilder screen only after cutover.
Sequence coexistence, testing, deployment, and support so legacy and modern experiences can run safely in parallel.
Continuously support approved partner integrations throughout migration, whether they use APIs or data access.
For each journey, decide whether to reimagine the experience or migrate it largely as is.

exact_text_nodes: React entry points during the PowerBuilder transition

West Monroe currently sees three potential paths forward for maintaining PowerBuilder screens in parallel with modernizing the user interface to be a modern web stack. We currently recommend redirecting users towards a browser based application; however, the exact approach will be validated during Phase 0.
Retains the Eaglesoft window. Use only when the installed PowerBuilder runtime supports the required behavior and the adoption value is clear.
Users open a practice network URL without installing or updating a desktop application. This is currently our preferred pilot for a bounded journey with limited native device needs.

A React UI can run in Electron, Tauri, or a .NET WebView2 shell. Useful for printing and tighter device access, but it may require an added workstation install. Phase 0 will assess how much native integration is needed.

Work with Patterson to select one pilot route and test the assumptions that matter for that journey. Assess runtime behavior, identity, printing, imaging, device access, deployment, recovery, and user effort.
Current belief: browser or PWA offers the easiest user access.
Phase 0 can assess Vue, Svelte, Angular, or Blazor/.NET if alternatives to React are considered
Domain operations, authorization, and transaction control
Governed PostgreSQL and related practice data
Phase 0. Work with Patterson to select one route to test. Use user effort, runtime compatibility, printing, device needs, deployment support, and recovery evidence to choose the pilot.

exact_text_nodes: Journey based PowerBuilder migration and retirement
Modernize a complete staff or customer journey, then retire the PowerBuilder components that served it.
Document the customer or staff outcome and its current execution path.
Link screens, DataWindows, event logic, SQL, stored procedures, integrations, devices, and existing test coverage to the journey.
Make the product decision first. Preserve an experience that still works. Improve workflows that need material change. Sequence the journey later when a dependency blocks a responsible move.
Build the chosen experience, not just new interface technology. React uses shared business operations for authorization, transaction behavior, and data access.
Integrate migration with automated behavior and performance tests. Use high-confidence evidence to confirm supportability, then remove the PowerBuilder dependencies the journey replaces.
Acceptance follows the journey: correct business outcome, dependable performance, and a supportable release.
Should this journey preserve today’s experience, materially improve it, or move later?
PowerBuilder exit occurs journey by journey, with no unowned legacy dependency left behind.

exact_text_nodes: Modernization follows a standard lifecycle from strategy through sustained value.
Rationalize, Build, and Sustain organize connected subphases, each with a clear purpose and value contribution.
Decide what should change and why
Define the business outcome and questions that justify action.
Establish how work, systems, risks, and dependencies operate today.
Test future process and experience options before target design hardens.
Select dispositions, economics, roadmap, and the first investable wave.
Turn high-level plans into target processes, architecture, and working prototypes.
Create bounded software and integration increments from approved rules and decisions.
Prove parity, controls, performance, and acceptance with traceable evidence.
Move data, operations, and people through controlled release waves.
Establish ownership, service levels, observability, security, and cost control.
Keep knowledge and the product backlog current so the capability improves with measured performance.
FOUR THREADS SHAPE EVERY PHASE GATE AND DELIVERY DECISION
Business value & economics   •   Process & experience   •   People & change   •   Technology & delivery
Clear remaining dependencies, then retire legacy code, data paths, controls, contracts, and cost.

Integrated initial phase for modernization and assurance
One journey inventory guides architecture decisions, early delivery planning, and testing investment.
Connect every priority journey to its code and dependency chain, customer impact, release pain points, current test coverage, performance evidence, and deployment conditions.
Scan the codebase and map dependencies with Intellio Evolve, Codex, and engineer review. Inspect test assets, environments, data, telemetry, and machine profiles.
Interview product, engineering, quality, and support. Rank journeys by customer value, release pain, risk, and dependency readiness.
Confirm the on premise UI, service, data, deployment, and operational patterns. Test the fit on selected journey candidates.
Reuse and strengthen existing automation. Establish a controlled baseline for a priority workflow and connect experience timing to technical evidence for diagnosis.
EVIDENCE TO PROCEED, RESCOPE, OR STOP
Patterson leaves the initial phase with a tested direction for the next delivery increments.
Tool assisted analysis speeds the work. Engineers and Patterson leaders retain design, quality, security, and release authority.

exact_text_nodes: Confirm system access, environments, tooling, and data; conduct onboarding and kickoff workshop
Assess the current architecture and active modernization initiatives
Inventory user journeys, queries, PowerBuilder screens, dependencies, reusable tests, and data
Prioritize the catalog and select the pilot journey
Finalize target architecture, implementation plan, and acceptable test standard
Prepare pilot backlog, environments, baseline data, instrumentation, and regression harness
Modernize the selected journey on the target architecture; build, test, and iterate
Run performance baseline/pilot and regression testing against the selected journey
Roadmap and prioritize the remaining journey catalog into implementation waves
Prepare pod onboarding documentation, backlog, dependencies, and technical plans
Recurring: Governance, architecture/test decisions, risk management, and stakeholder readouts
Phase 0 aligns the current state, target architecture, and test standard before a two-week pilot,
then roadmaps remaining journeys and prepares modernization pods to launch
Pre-week confirms access and onboarding readiness; detailed dependencies will be refined during kickoff

Our client’s core product is built on legacy technologies and has been customized over time, increasing maintenance costs while losing market share and delaying innovation. Previous modernization efforts have taken multiple years and have failed due to the complexity of 4GL code transformation and migration strategies.
Used an AI-first approach to evaluate the codebase and plan the strategic rewrite of one of the core modules

Evolve alongside commercial AI tooling (Claude Code, AWS Kiro) to build a rapid prototype of a full rewrite to a modern language (Java / Spring) in a fraction of the time it would have taken with traditional approaches
Best outcomes were driven by our approach using domain-driven design, technical specs, architecture steering files to guide AI agents with implementation
Building Smarter Solutions to Modernize Legacy Code with AI
Accelerated understanding, planning, and refactoring efforts of a legacy platform
Planning the rebuild strategy was complex and the team couldn’t agree on a starting point. Using our agentic modernization approach supported by
Evolve, we condensed an activity that had taken months into days
A big thank you to you and the West Monroe team. We highly appreciate the partnership and all that WM has contributed to our current success. It would not have been possible without the team's work.
One of the platforms modules (~200K LoC) was targeted for transformation and performed inside a single sprint, an activity that would have taken 10 times longer using traditional approaches

Drove ~10x improvement in architecture team productivity by creating a shared, end-to-end view of the architecture and dependencies—reducing discovery time and rework so the team could deliver more with less.
Produced a highly granular build plan that would serve as the foundation for next-gen code generation
Created a repeatable, agentic workflow to serve as the go-forward development process
Enabled ongoing refinement with the leadership team to fine-tune the build based on their domain expertise

exact_paragraphs.text: International Wire Group, a copper wire manufacturer, relied on a decades-old VAX-based mainframe system across QC, customer management, AP documents, and scheduling, creating friction for factory floor and back-office teams alike. We designed Volt ERP, a modern MUI-based platform, establishing reusable patterns like split panels, drawer editing, and multi-step forms across each domain. The result is a scalable, documented design system and an AI-assisted design-to-dev workflow that keeps specs and engineering in sync as the platform grows.

exact_paragraphs.text: Tyler is a leader on West Monroe’s Healthcare M&A team, focusing on payer, provider and healthcare IT sectors. During his 10+ years at West Monroe, he’s supported 400+ transactions and has helped hundreds of private equity firms and portfolio companies assess, plan, and implement technology initiatives that advance growth objectives.

Tyler is a leader on West Monroe’s Healthcare M&A team, focusing on payer, provider and healthcare IT sectors

During his 10+ years at West Monroe, he’s supported 400+ transactions and has helped hundreds of private equity firms and portfolio companies assess, plan, and implement technology initiatives that advance growth objectives.

Tyler brings hands-on experience across multi-site, post-acute, and home-based services; revenue cycle and payment integrity; payer services and cost containment; EMR/PMS platforms; and value-based primary care models.

In 2025, he was named to M&A Advisors’ Emerging Leaders list and is a frequent source on healthcare M&A for CNBC, Axios, Modern Healthcare, and other leading outlets. Prior to joining WM, Tyler managed contact center operations and technology for a health system.
A proud Indiana native, Tyler grew up during the heyday of Indiana college and pro basketball and enjoys catching a game when he can.
As a former healthcare operator, Tyler helps clients navigate complex and emerging industry dynamics to identify solutions that move the needle on cost, quality, and outcomes.

Leveraging decades of consulting experience, Dhaval specializes in helping software, technology, and IT services companies capitalize on emerging trends and drive growth. He has partnered with clients to create and grow new products, maximize value through M&A transactions, drive cross-functional initiatives, enable profitable growth through digital transformation, and transition to subscription-based business models. Dhaval energizes and aligns teams around growth opportunities and mentors junior consultants. Prior to joining West Monroe, he was a managing director at Waterstone Group. He holds degrees from Mumbai University and Indiana University.
A husband and father, Dhaval enjoys hiking, biking, and traveling. He has spent time in more than 25 countries and has lived and worked on three continents.

Dhaval led the transformation of an enterprise software company’s operating model, tripling subscription revenue. He transformed a SaaS provider’s customer engagement model, increasing retention rates, and launched subscription offerings delivering over $200 million in value.

exact_paragraphs.text:
Erik is a seasoned software engineer, entrepreneur, and leader who leverages innovative technology to drive business value. He led a $20 million technology roadmap project, enhancing a client’s risk modeling and cutting technology costs by over $10 million annually. As the executive technical lead for West Monroe’s AI Lab, he spearheaded the rollout of an internal AI chat platform and client-facing AI accelerators. Erik frequently speaks at industry events and hosts West Monroe’s “This is Digital” podcast. With extensive experience in software engineering, cloud computing, and AI, he leads the engineering team in PXEL practice. Erik holds a bachelor’s degree from the University
of Illinois.

Erik is a seasoned software engineer, entrepreneur, and leader who leverages innovative technology to drive business value. He led a $20 million technology roadmap project, enhancing a client’s risk modeling and cutting technology costs by over $10 million annually. As the executive technical lead for West Monroe’s AI Lab, he spearheaded the rollout of an internal AI chat platform and client-facing AI accelerators. Erik frequently speaks at industry events and hosts West Monroe’s “This is Digital” podcast. With extensive experience in software engineering, cloud computing, and AI, he leads the engineering team in PXEL practice. Erik holds a bachelor’s degree from the University
Erik lives in Chicago with his family, enjoys music, and blends artistic expression with math and science through piano.
Erik volunteers at St. Francis Xavier School, leading the Technology Committee; West Monroe designs their annual report.
